description: Literal positive, negative, and canonical-form vectors for the DataPulse canonical JSON form.
bom_policy: No UTF-8 BOM; no trailing newline.

positive.name: scalars_and_nesting
positive.note: Keys are sorted, booleans/null are lowercase, arrays keep their order, and no whitespace is emitted.

positive.name: unicode_preserved_as_utf8
positive.note: ensure_ascii=False keeps non-ASCII as UTF-8 octets; the emoji is an astral-plane character (surrogate pair in UTF-16).

positive.name: large_integers_exact
positive.note: Integers round-trip exactly even when they exceed binary64 or signed-64-bit range; no float coercion is allowed.

positive.name: empty_and_falsey_values
positive.note: Empty containers and falsey values are preserved; none may be dropped or coerced.

negative.name: bom_prefixed
negative.reason: A UTF-8 BOM changes the first signed byte (EF BB BF) and therefore the digest.
negative.note: The wrong bytes are the canonical text with a BOM prepended.

negative.name: trailing_newline_appended
negative.reason: A trailing newline is not part of the signed bytes; the newline written to an envelope file is formatting only.

negative.name: keys_reordered
negative.reason: A permutation of the canonical key order is a different byte string even though it is the same object.
negative.note: The wrong bytes are a dumps(sort_keys=False) rendering of the same four members in reverse sorted order.

negative.name: key_order_in_equivalent_object
negative.reason: An equivalent object keeps its insertion order and nested order, so a serialiser that does not sort (or sorts only the top level) emits different bytes.

negative.name: default_separator_whitespace
negative.reason: json.dumps defaults to separators (', ', ': '); the spaces are insignificant JSON but significant to a digest.
negative.note: Canonical separators are (',', ':') with no spaces.

negative.name: indent_rendering
negative.reason: Pretty-printed JSON with indentation is a different byte string; signed material must never be indented.

negative.name: float_value
negative.reason: A non-integer number has more than one JSON spelling; 100.0 and 1e2 parse to the same double but are different bytes. Floats are prohibited in signed payloads.

negative.name: float_valued_integer_vs_integer
negative.reason: 1.0 and 1 compare equal in Python but are different JSON types and different bytes; a language that preserves the integer loses the decimal marker.

negative.name: nan_value
negative.reason: NaN is not valid RFC 8259 JSON. Python json.dumps emits it anyway, and a non-conformant parser may silently coerce it to null; both must fail closed.
negative.note: payload_json is parsed leniently to materialise float('nan'); strict parsing of it and of the canonical bytes must both raise.

negative.name: duplicate_keys
negative.reason: A lenient parser keeps the last value and hides the duplicate; the canonical form has no way to express it, so parsing must reject it.

negative.name: ensure_ascii_rendering
negative.reason: ensure_ascii=True rewrites non-ASCII as \uXXXX escapes; the signature must cover the UTF-8 octets instead.

canonical_form.name: key_insertion_order_irrelevant
canonical_form.note: Two dict literals with opposite insertion orders.

canonical_form.name: nested_construction_paths
canonical_form.note: Nested objects are sorted at every level; arrays keep their order.

canonical_form.name: parsed_json_path_agrees
canonical_form.note: One path is a Python literal; the other is parsed JSON text with whitespace and a different key order.

canonical_form.name: unicode_construction_paths
canonical_form.note: A literal UTF-8 string and an escaped \u00e9 both decode to the same value, so canonical bytes are identical.
